text:
elaine: heads-up — we've got a spike of 502/504s on hosted inference since ~09:12 UTC. multiple customers reporting timeouts and 5xx in the gateway.

elaine: example: API -> /v1/generate returns 504 after 30s, X-Request-ID: req_8f3a2. logs show `upstream request timed out` and repeated `kv get failed` errors.

jess-support: customer reported 30% error rate, started ~09:10, slow responses for embedding and chat calls. they attached curl response with 502 body.

ryan-oncall: looking. initial read: gateway is blocking on cache reads (prefix/KV). seeing redis connection errors in the gateway pod logs. hitting infra to confirm backend cache status.

cache-bot: ALERT: redis-cluster-prod region us-west-2 latency >1000ms across >50% nodes. connections dropping. (auto-detected by cache-watch).

marta-infra: confirmed — cloud provider reported transient network partition to elasticache cluster 172.31.12.5/172.31.12.6 for ~3m starting 09:09 UTC. some nodes marked FAIL in cluster.

sam-sre: that explains the KV timeouts. our prefix caching layer doesn't degrade gracefully; it blocks requests while trying multiple replicas. Need immediate mitigations: 1) bypass cache for critical routes 2) switch cache client pool to fail-fast 3) enable fallback path to cold model fetch.

elaine: support impact: customers see gateway 502/504. Some retries are causing token consumption. Billing team pinged. Can we rate-limit retries?

ryan-oncall: implemented temporary rule to return 503 with Retry-After for high latency routes to avoid token burn — pushed policy to gateway at 09:18 UTC.

sam-sre: commands I ran:
```
# check gateway logs for kv errors
kubectl -n prod logs deploy/gateway -c gateway --since=20m | grep "kv get failed" | tail -n 50

# probe redis latency
redis-cli -h cache-primary.usw2.redwood.internal --latency -i 0.5

# check cache cluster health
aws elasticache describe-cache-clusters --cache-cluster-id redis-prod --show-cache-node-info
```

marta-infra: provider already completed failover at 09:21 and most nodes are back. but we still see higher p99 latency (200-400ms) compared to normal ~10ms. cache client is configured to do blocking multi-get across prefixes which amplifies impact.

jess-support: any quick repro steps so we can tell customers? they asked how to workaround from their side.

sam-sre: repro: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-2-medium","input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate ; you'll see 502/504 when cache calls block. Add header X-Bypass-Cache: true to force cold path (temporary).

elaine: sharing that with customers now. also adding note to docs that they can set `X-Bypass-Cache` if they see persistent KV-related errors.

marta-infra: long-term fix items noted: 1) change cache client to fail-fast with async background refresh 2) add circuit breaker around cache calls 3) increase observability for per-prefix latency 4) evaluate multi-region read replicas for prefix cache.

ryan-oncall: I opened an incident ticket INC-2023-4922 and assigned to eng-runtime + infra. ETA for mitigation rollout (fail-fast + circuit breaker) is ~3 hours if no blockers.

sam-sre: rolling change to gateway config to set cache client timeout lower (from 500ms -> 100ms) and to short-circuit on repeated errors. will monitor. pushed at 09:30 UTC.

cache-bot: METRIC: kv_client_errors spike from 2/min -> 340/min between 09:10-09:18. error type: connection timeout.

marta-infra: provider incident root cause says transient network congestion to elasticache due to noisy neighbor on host cluster. they recommend moving to cluster-mode with stronger isolation. I'll scope migration plan.

jess-support: customers notified with status update. collecting a list of affected orgs for credits if we need to.

elaine: postmortem checklist for when incident is closed: collect request IDs, tie to customer reports, compute excess token/billing impact, and ship postmortem and RCA.

sam-sre: immediate logs to gather for RCA: gateway logs (kv errors + request ids), cache client traces (prefix key list), redis server slowlog and client connection logs, and packet drops from infra.

ryan-oncall: next steps summary: (1) monitor for error rate returning to baseline (2) complete gateway timeout/circuit-breaker release (in flight) (3) infra to schedule redis cluster remediation/migration (4) support to coordinate customer comms.

elaine: thanks all. I'm keeping the thread updated with customer replies. adding link to the incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2023-4922

jess-support: small note — if customers ask for immediate workaround: advise setting `X-Bypass-Cache: true` or reduce parallelism. both reduce cache pressure.

marta-infra: marking this as high priority for infra follow-up, creating infra-epic for prefix-cache hardening.

sam-sre: will reopen if we see another spike. good job moving quickly. :thumbsup:
